prompt: CHALLENGE: Styrene oxide (PhCH-CH₂-O, phenyl-substituted epoxide) opens with methanol. Under ACIDIC conditions, OMe goes to the BENZYLIC carbon. Under BASIC conditions, OMe goes to the TERMINAL CH₂. Why does the regiochemistry flip?

options.label: In acid, the TS has significant carbocation character at the benzylic C (stabilized by Ph), so the nucleophile attacks there. In base, SN2-like attack prefers the less hindered terminal CH₂ (standard steric control).
Different C–O bonds break in each case.

explanation: This is the textbook demonstration: acid makes the more-substituted (or stabilized) C the attack site because its C–O is more cleaved in the TS. Base makes the LESS-substituted C the attack site because sterics win in an SN2-like TS. Styrene oxide is dramatic because Ph strongly stabilizes the benzylic cation.
